review_output.summary: `convertLinks` now runs on every text delta, even when web search is off, and its internal buffer is never flushed. Any text after a `[` that isn't a complete `[text](url)` link gets held back and lost when the stream ends.
review_output.failure_scenario: Web search is off and the model writes code such as `arr[i] = 1` followed by more text, or a JSON array like `["a","b"]`. convertLinks sets its safePoint at that `[` and keeps everything after it in its module-global buffer. No later chunk releases it, so the end of the answer never reaches TEXT_DELTA or TEXT_COMPLETE.

review_output.summary: `content` is built from link-converted, buffered text and then passed to `processToolUses`/`parseAndCallTools`. Prompt-based MCP tool calls whose JSON contains `[` get cut off or rewritten.
review_output.failure_scenario: The model emits `<tool_use>{"name":"x","arguments":{"ids":[1,2]}}</tool_use>`. convertLinks holds everything from `[1,2]` onward, so `content` is missing the closing tags. parseAndCallTools finds no valid tool call and the tool never runs. The mangled text is also pushed back into reqMessages as the assistant message.

review_output.summary: `convertLinks` is called without `resetCounter`, so its module-global counter, URL map and buffer are never reset between responses (the old code passed `isFirstChunk`).
review_output.failure_scenario: Leftover text in the buffer from the previous message, or from the previous tool-call round, is prepended to the first text of the next response. Citation numbers keep counting up across messages (the second answer starts at [5] instead of [1]).

review_output.summary: TEXT_COMPLETE, processToolUses and BLOCK_COMPLETE now run only inside the `finish` case. If the stream ends without a finish_reason chunk, or the user pauses, the block is never completed.
review_output.failure_scenario: The user hits pause: `openAIChunkToTextDelta` breaks without yielding `finish`. Some OpenAI-compatible providers also close the stream without a finish_reason. In both cases no TEXT_COMPLETE or BLOCK_COMPLETE is emitted, the message stays in the streaming/processing state, usage and metrics are lost, and pending tool calls never run. The old code always ran these after the loop.

review_output.summary: The provider-specific link conversions were removed (`convertLinksToOpenRouter`, `convertLinksToZhipu`, `convertLinksToHunyuan` with search_info results, and the annotations path). Only generic `convertLinks` remains.
review_output.failure_scenario: With web search on and a Zhipu model, `[ref_1]` markers are no longer turned into superscript citations. Hunyuan search citations are no longer mapped to `search_info.search_results` URLs. OpenRouter citation formatting regresses. All of these now render raw or wrongly converted markers.

review_output.summary: The TransformStream has no `flush` handler. Text held in `buffer` because it might be the start of a `<think>`/`</think>` tag is dropped when the stream ends.
review_output.failure_scenario: The model's answer ends with `x <` or `<t`, or a reasoning block ends with an unterminated partial `</thi`. getPotentialStartIndex keeps that tail in `buffer`, the stream closes, and the last characters never get published.

review_output.summary: THINKING_COMPLETE is emitted only when a text-delta arrives after reasoning. The old checks for `###Response` and `hasReasoningContent` were removed, so a reasoning-only turn, or a GLM-Zero-style `###Response` separator, never closes the thinking block.
review_output.failure_scenario: A model streams reasoning_content and then finishes with a tool call or empty content, or glm-zero-preview uses `###Response`. No THINKING_COMPLETE is sent, the thinking block stays 'in progress', and time_thinking_millsec is reported as 0.

review_output.summary: The `readableStreamAsyncIterable` iterator has no `return()`, and `asyncGeneratorToReadableStream` has no `cancel()`. Early exit or an error never releases the reader lock or closes the generator/underlying SDK stream.
review_output.failure_scenario: If onChunk or processToolUses throws inside the `for await`, the reader stays locked and the upstream generator, along with the OpenAI HTTP stream, is never returned or aborted. The connection and generator leak.

review_output.summary: `getAppropriateTag` is dead branching: every path returns `reasoningTags[0]`, so the `reasoning` tag entry is unused. The `!isEmpty(finishReason)` check inside `case 'finish'` is always true, and `currentTime` is redeclared, shadowing the outer one.
review_output.failure_scenario: Readers will assume claude or other models get a different tag, or that `<reasoning>` tags are extracted, but they never are. It is redundant code that misleads maintainers. Replace it with a single `{ tagName: 'think', separator: '\n' }` constant and drop the redundant check and the shadowed variable.

review_output.summary: `wrapGenerate` builds a RegExp from an unescaped `tagName`, and nothing calls it. It also duplicates the existing `thinkTagProcessor`/`findThinkingProcessor` logic in BaseProvider/utils/formats, which is now orphaned.
review_output.failure_scenario: A tagName containing regex metacharacters would produce a wrong match. As it stands this is unused code, and there are now two parallel think-tag parsers (ThoughtProcessor and the middleware) to maintain. Remove `wrapGenerate`, and either use the existing processors or delete them.
